author: unknown
title: Runtime diffing is client-side: the SSG embeds a build timestamp, browser JS fetches comments newer than that timestamp and appends them.

author: unknown
title: Client-side script has zero dependencies, uses textContent exclusively (never innerHTML) to prevent XSS by construction.

author: unknown
title: Two auth keys: SITE_KEY (public, embedded in comment form) identifies the site. ADMIN_KEY (secret, Bearer token) protects destructive operations like delete.

author: unknown
title: Import path must be compatible with the legacy jcomments SQLite database schema. Field mapping: reader_name→author, comment→text, created_at→createdAt, id preserved.

author: unknown
title: Storage format is one JSON file per page in object storage, keyed by URL path. No database, no schema migrations.

author: unknown
title: Default implementation uses Cloudflare Workers + R2. Chosen for permanent generous free tiers (100K req/day, 10GB storage, zero egress) and good DX.

author: unknown
title: Spam prevention uses honeypot field plus optional Cloudflare Turnstile (free). No Akismet dependency.

author: unknown
title: Spam is silently discarded, never queued for review. No moderation workflow.

author: unknown
title: Feature set is deliberately minimal: plain text comments, spam filtering, deletion. No threads, voting, replies, email notifications, or moderation dashboard.

author: unknown
title: No vendor lock-in. The runtime and storage layer must be portable to other cloud providers (AWS, GCP, etc.) or to a plain Node.js server. Core logic stays provider-agnostic.

author: unknown
title: Must run entirely within cloud provider free tiers for a typical personal blog.

author: unknown
title: Minimal infrastructure: a single cloud function and an object store. No databases, no queues, no always-on servers.

author: unknown
title: The publisher owns all comment data. No third-party storage, no vendor lock-in on the data layer.

author: unknown
title: Comments are baked into static HTML at build time. The browser only fetches comments added after the last build. This ensures comments survive outages and load instantly.

author: unknown
title: This system serves a single personal/small-audience static blog. No multi-tenancy, no accounts, no dashboard.
